findings.correction: Gleam owns a finite reviewed service capability and stable request-to-canonical-plan/task mapping through existing Sa-plan bridge, not raw Sa-plan SQL. Specify deterministic create/reconcile, claim actual worker/attempt, acquire derived coordinator task resource, current clock/boot fences, pre/post read validation, durable result/outbox binding, complete and release. Reconcile crashes between ledger and Sa-plan transitions without invented completion. Reject expired/missing/blocked/wrong-attempt authority. Native OCaml is bounded transport/store IO only; authentication/scheduling/verdicts stay in Gleam.

findings.correction: Use a process-lifetime OS/service ownership lock plus admitted runtime:telegram-bridge coordinator lease with renewal and boot/epoch checks; close/stop intake and dispatch on loss. BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes short DB transitions only and must not span network calls. Atomically claim pending inbox/outbox rows with owner, attempt and epoch using conditional transitions; define stale claim recovery. Fence each network dispatch and classify in-flight lease loss as uncertain; a lease alone cannot cancel an already sent HTTP request.

findings.correction: Persist the bounded sanitized response, destination, request/task/result digest and ordered chunk identities before sending; use stable logical IDs scoped by bot/update, enforce duplicate-content equality, and record individual send attempts. Commit SENDING before IO. Success requires parsed BotAPI ok=true and matching message identity; crash after SENDING or unknown HTTP outcome becomes UNCERTAIN and is not automatically retried. Local request_id is not remote send deduplication. Same-ID retry needs proof the prior attempt was not sent or explicitly authorized reconciliation acknowledging possible duplication. Do not claim at-most-once delivery from bookkeeping; describe durable intake and no-blind-retry behavior precisely.

findings.area: Privacy, bounds and legacy ingress containment
findings.correction: Authenticate before conversation memory, parsing directives, model evaluation, reactions or relay. Logs contain approved IDs/status/error codes only, not truncated private text, token-bearing URLs or raw error bodies. Private ledger0600/directory0700 stores only bounded required envelope/response fields with declared retention, queue capacity, payload size, timeout and backpressure. Disable legacy shared-key Telegram execution, quality-evaluation publication and parallel bridge polling/sending in the scoped cutover. Never delete shared keys; per-ID wakeups are hints and ledger state is authoritative.
